The gaming crash of 1983? Basically, the early 1980 saw games for the early console market (Atari 2600/5200, Coleco Vision, and then some others) being produced and published in far greater quantities that an already over-satured market could handle. Even worse, most of these games were poorly-coded garbage because publishers knew most customers had no way to judge the potential game beyond its freaking cover art (leaving aside some of the still rare print gaming magazines).

At some point, the consumerbase simply had enough and quite plainly stopped buying games (mind you that gaming consoles were absurdly costly back in the day due to lower production numbers and other factors). For an industry which was entirely built around the seemingly ceaseless economic growth of its respective department, this very quickly turned into a death blow (with an effective drop in sales revenue of about 97% (!) ).

Nintendo and its Nintendo Entertainment system eventually revitalized the market because a) Nintendo very intentionally marketed itself as a children's toy, and b) Nintendo used and still uses relatively tight quality controls, whereas Atari & Co. would literally sell a turd on a plate on its customers so long as it would get some cash.
